paper.title: Search strategies to identify observational studies in MEDLINE and Embase

evidence.paraphrase: Cochrane methodology review of studies using a relative-recall approach to compare the sensitivity and precision of search filters against reference standards.
Reports filter sensitivity (48-100%) and precision against reference sets drawn from systematic reviews.

reviews.rationale: The review directly concerns validating literature-search strategies by relative recall against benchmark reference standards, which is the core of the search_validation_reachability role. It also supplies empirical sensitivity/precision precedents.

paper.title: A practical guide to evaluating sensitivity of literature search strings for systematic reviews using relative recall

evidence.paraphrase: Presents a procedure for estimating relative recall of a search string from a predefined set of benchmark publications.
Surveys published reviews and finds search-sensitivity validation is rarely conducted or reported.

reviews.rationale: This is a direct methodological account of benchmark-set relative recall for search validation, matching the role's purpose and terms almost exactly. It can anchor the definition of reachability/recall checks in the manuscript.

paper.title: Introducing PALETTE: an iterative method for conducting a literature search for a review in palliative care

evidence.paraphrase: PALETTE validates the search strategy recurrently against 'golden bullets' that must be included, combined with pearl growing and citation tracking.
Components are repeated until no new articles qualify, an iterative search process that changes the search state.
Evaluation is a comparison on two palliative-care reviews, so empirical evidence is limited.

reviews.rationale: Golden-bullet validation is a benchmark-set check of search sensitivity, fitting this role directly, and the iterative citation-tracking loop bridges to the bibliography-as-research-state and iterative retrieval themes. The empirical comparison is small, but the method contribution is clear from the abstract.

paper.title: Information retrieval in systematic reviews: a case study of the crime prevention literature

evidence.paraphrase: Reports empirical results on balancing sensitivity and precision and estimates database overlap in a systematic crime-prevention search.
Framed as a practical how-to guide for systematic searching, recommending complementary tactics for studies without shared vocabulary.

reviews.rationale: The paper provides an empirical precedent for search sensitivity/precision trade-offs and the limits of database reachability, which supports the role. It is a practice guide rather than a formal validation method, so the fit is partial.

paper.title: Data extraction methods for systematic review (semi)automation: Update of a living systematic review

evidence.paraphrase: A living systematic review of methods for (semi)automated data extraction (e.g., PICO entities) from clinical study reports.
Its own search of PubMed, arXiv, OpenAlex and dblp is procedural; it does not evaluate search sensitivity, relative recall or reachability.
Overlap with the role is limited to systematic-review and recall vocabulary.

reviews.rationale: The contribution concerns data extraction after studies are found, not validating whether searches reach relevant records. It does not fit the search-validation role or other inclusion-boundary themes closely enough to retain.
